package_info.package_versions: All versions containing CVE-2021-44228 or CVE-2021-45046 vulnerabilities
package_info.why_malicious: Packages that directly include vulnerable Log4j code (either as shaded classes or as fat jars) are susceptible to remote code execution via Log4Shell. This risk persists even if Log4j is not explicitly listed as a dependency, as hidden inclusion bypasses standard dependency scanning and exposes applications to exploitation through malicious JNDI lookups in log messages.

execution_context.file_location: shaded Log4j classes within the package JAR (e.g., org/apache/logging/log4j/core/lookup/JndiLookup.class)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code evaluates user-controlled log message content using the JndiLookup class, processes JNDI lookup strings, and initiates network requests to resolve remote resources, resulting in potential arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The JndiLookup class enables evaluation of JNDI expressions in log messages, allowing attackers to inject references to remote resources (e.g., LDAP/HTTP endpoints) that can return malicious payloads for execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard logging libraries should not interpret or resolve remote code or execute user-supplied input within log messages.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups are legitimately used in enterprise Java for resource resolution, but not within the context of log message evaluation or user-controlled input.
key_indicators: JNDI string parsing and evaluation during log message processing
Network requests initiated as a result of log message content

execution_context.file_location: log4j-core-*.jar (vulnerable version) bundled as a fat jar within the application artifact

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: log4j-core-2.x.x.jar (vulnerable version) bundled inside the artifact
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the bundled vulnerable log4j-core jar processes log messages, evaluates JNDI-based expressions, and can initiate outbound network requests to attacker-controlled servers, enabling remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Including a known-vulnerable log4j-core jar exposes the application to the Log4Shell exploit, allowing attackers to trigger remote code execution via crafted log messages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Application artifacts should not contain outdated or vulnerable third-party libraries, especially those with critical remote code execution vulnerabilities.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Fat jars are commonly used to package dependencies for deployment, but all included libraries should be up-to-date and free of known vulnerabilities.
key_indicators: Bundled log4j-core jar with version <= 2.15.0 inside application artifact
No corresponding dependency entry for Log4j in build files (hidden inclusion)
Artifact contains the full vulnerable log4j-core jar

attack_chain.action: Vulnerable Log4j code is included directly in the application artifact, either as shaded classes or as a bundled jar.
attack_chain.leads_to: The application is exposed to Log4Shell exploit vectors, even if Log4j is not declared as a dependency.

attack_chain.action: At runtime, an attacker sends a crafted log message containing a malicious JNDI lookup string to the application.
attack_chain.leads_to: The vulnerable Log4j code evaluates the JNDI lookup in the log message.

attack_chain.action: The JNDI lookup triggers a remote resource fetch (e.g., via LDAP or HTTP), potentially loading and executing attacker-controlled code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution occurs on the victim system, granting the attacker control.

behavioral_signatures: Detection of org.apache.logging.log4j.core.lookup.JndiLookup class within application or dependency JARs
Evaluation of JNDI strings (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://...}) in log message processing
Outbound network requests initiated as a direct result of log message content
file_indicators: Presence of org/apache/logging/log4j/core/lookup/JndiLookup.class in application or dependency JARs
Absence of corresponding Log4j dependency entry in build files despite presence of Log4j classes
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP or HTTP requests initiated during log message processing
Connections to external or attacker-controlled domains immediately following log events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Perform deep scanning of application artifacts to identify the presence of vulnerable Log4j classes or bundled jars, regardless of declared dependencies. Analyze log message processing code for JNDI lookup evaluation. Monitor for unexpected outbound LDAP/HTTP requests triggered by log events. Use tools capable of inspecting both direct dependencies and embedded (shaded or bundled) code.
